title: Public-health workers report worsening strain, political interference, and younger-worker exit risk
source_unit: de Beaumont Foundation and ASTHO PH WINS Pulse Check, March 2026; 4,827 public-health employees responding from 13,486 PH WINS 2024 respondents
geography: United States; state and local governmental public-health workforce

denominator.unit: employees completing the PH WINS Pulse Check

burnout_worse.unit: percent saying feelings of burnout worsened since PH WINS 2024

stress_worse.unit: percent saying stress was worse or much worse since 2024

young_worker_burnout_worse.unit: percent of employees age 35 and younger

observations.method: Online pulse survey distributed to PH WINS 2024 respondents; descriptive comparison of reported workplace conditions since the 2024 administration.
observations.uncertainty: The pulse check is a follow-up among prior respondents with a 36% completion rate; it is not a fresh probability sample of all public-health workers, and reported change does not establish cause or clinical burnout diagnosis.
observations.subgroup: State and local public-health employees by age, with younger employees defined as age 35 and younger.
observations.counterinterpretation: Worsening reported strain may reflect changing expectations, news, work demands, or recall; it does not mean every employee experienced deterioration or that staffing loss necessarily followed.

observations.period: 2024–March 2026; politics and budgets in public-health work units

denominator.unit: employees completing the PH WINS Pulse Check

work_unit_budget_worse.unit: percent saying budget is worse than in 2024

observations.method: PH WINS Pulse Check descriptive questions on external political conditions and work-unit budgets.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not disclose all question wording, subgroup precision, or the specific political and budget mechanisms; perceived influence is not an audited measure of policy interference or fiscal change.
observations.subgroup: State and local public-health employees and their work units.
observations.counterinterpretation: Political attention can sometimes increase resources or accountability; a negative influence rating may reflect conflict, uncertainty, mission change, communication, or broader fiscal conditions rather than one actor’s intervention.

denominator.unit: employees completing the PH WINS Pulse Check

under_35_plan_to_leave_next_year.unit: percent of employees age 35 and younger

observations.method: PH WINS Pulse Check self-reported intention-to-leave and retirement measures, compared with 2024 where stated.
observations.uncertainty: Intentions are not departures; age groups have different career stages and denominators, and the follow-up sample may differ from the full 2024 respondent pool.
observations.subgroup: State and local public-health employees by age.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some planned exits may be internal transfers, retirement timing changes, or responses to temporary conditions; high younger-worker exit intent can coexist with strong commitment among those who remain.

denominator.unit: employees completing the PH WINS Pulse Check

advancement_opportunities_worse.unit: percent reporting opportunities for advancement worsened since 2024

job_instability_reason_for_leaving.unit: percent among those reporting worsening advancement and citing a reason for leaving

observations.method: PH WINS Pulse Check descriptive comparison of advancement opportunities and reasons for leaving.
observations.uncertainty: The second measure is conditional on a subgroup and does not establish that job instability caused an actual departure; public summary details on item nonresponse and subgroup denominators are limited.
observations.subgroup: Public-health employees reporting advancement changes and leaving considerations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Limited advancement may reflect flatter public organizations, hiring freezes, budget constraints, or changed expectations; career development can occur through training or lateral mobility not captured by promotion.

related_sources.claim: PH WINS 2024 survey context and methodology family.
Related system-capacity record; it is not pooled with these worker-level pulse estimates.

boundary: This record captures worker-reported changes in burnout, stress, political influence, budgets, retention, retirement, advancement, and job instability among PH WINS follow-up respondents. It does not establish causal workforce exits, represent every public-health employee, measure agency performance, or infer community health outcomes.
